manual_checks_passed: Observer import is inert; live Runtime was never instantiated during review.
Root wrapper defaults to inert mode without clock or subprocess calls; verified with prohibited-call fixtures.
Exact teal hostname, boot, saved operation, original tool session, owner directory, and 39 historical PID sequence are bound.
All 14 contract local-evidence SHA256 values matched accepted local scalar/control files.
All 39 historical full projected PID/start/available argv and ancestry rows matched accepted evaluation, qualification, or collection metadata.
Original saved release, hard deadline, clock sample, worker command, and owner/timeout arguments are retained.
Duplicate and nonfinite JSON is rejected; non-object registry roots yield invalid coverage.
PID fields reject bool, nonintegers, out-of-range values; start ticks require positive bounded canonical ASCII decimal strings.
Terminal and registration identities are cross-checked; conflicting repeated owner or worker identities prevent scope expansion.
Missing terminal allows complete identity coverage from start and registration; missing original roles do not count as absent.
No registry-supplied paths are followed, and incomplete or contradictory registries cannot add arbitrary native PIDs.
Native reads are restricted to exact PID stat/cmdline paths plus the fixed boot and registry paths; no directory or process enumeration exists.
Read traversal uses no-follow directory descriptors, final nonblocking read-only opens, regular-file checks, finite byte caps, and before/after fstat mutation checks.
16 MiB registry cap permits ordinary 1.4 MiB terminal metadata; zero proc stat size cannot bypass the actual byte cap.
Proc stat parser supports spaces/parentheses in comm and validates native states and canonical numeric fields.
Present identities bracket cmdline with stat reads; start or ancestry changes produce unresolved observation states.
PID reuse is distinguished before cmdline reads, so unrelated process command lines are not read.
Zombie and orphaned original identities remain present; argv or ancestry changes never become absence.
Permission errors, malformed native metadata, and mid-read disappearance cannot establish stable absence.
Full native closure requires complete identities, both 42-PID absence rounds, unchanged registry bytes, and unchanged expected boot.
Recorded-identity absence including stable reuse remains distinct from the stricter all-PIDs-absent closure flag.
Unverified terminal claims never set scientific admission, remote execution success, or a new analysis clock/release.
Helper cooperatively checks a 12-second UTC/monotonic bound; remote command uses exact GNU timeout KILL 20s and isolated nonoptimized Python.
Shell quoting roundtrips exact observer source and arguments; original SSH alias/config, connection timeout, attempt count, and server-alive limits are preserved.
Root wrapper checks a reviewed manifest and directly matches the in-memory observer and contract bytes to their manifest SHA256 pins.
SSH input/output is nonblocking and byte-capped; root wrapper reserves cleanup/publication time within its cooperative 35-second bound.
Cleanup signals can target only the newly created local SSH group while its leader remains unreaped; original process signals are absent.
Local leader reaping is not described as descendant closure; descendant closure remains explicitly false.
Proxy accepts only canonical uncredentialed http://127.0.0.1:PORT, copies parent environment, sets child HTTPS_PROXY and https_proxy, removes child NO_PROXY and no_proxy, and leaves parent unchanged.
Proxy values are not logged; wrapper does not start/stop proxies or change SSH configuration, credentials, remote URLs, or TLS checks.
Publication budget field is explicitly pre-publication and followed by a post-write bound check; actual original tool exit remains required.
Handoff preserves expired allocation and censoring, disallows scientific admission/retry through this observer, and describes remaining operational prerequisites without creating a new phase.
